Springbok Homecoming

By: Stenette Grosskopf | Paid

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
They are the champions of the world... returning from an epic battle in France.

Unique Selling Point:
Once again the Springboks have inspired an entire country at a time when we might have felt somewhat hopeless about South Africa. In a series of nail-biting matches, the team showed tenacity and determination, to eventually lift the Webb Ellis trophy for the second time in a row.

On 31 October the team will return to SA, and ORT promises to be the scene of celebration and overwhelming pride, with thousands of supporters expected to welcome the Boks home.

Summary:
We celebrate the Springboks, showcasing their homecoming and find out what it took to become world champions...

And we take a brief look at the future. What is in store for the players and SA rugby...

Further information:
No idea what to expect at this stage -- It's a moving target.
Will film the homecoming
The press conference
Hopefully have access to them on Wed at Multichoice
And then the Jhb leg of their Victory Parade

Extra Budget Items:
Depending on when we can interview team members... we might need an extra presenter day. But I will try my best to avoid that.

Press Release:


A Champion’s Return
The Rugby World Cup Champions are home. In scenes reminiscent of the Springboks’ victorious return from the 2019 World Cup tournament in Japan, South Africans – loud and proud – rolled out the red carpet for our heroes at OR Tambo International Airport on Tuesday. Thousands of people, singing and dancing, celebrated the Boks’ triumph in lifting the Webb Ellis Cup for a historic fourth time, the first team to win back-to-back World Cup victories. Now, as skipper Siya Kolisi and his team continue their whirlwind tour with the coveted trophy, Carte Blanche examines how the Springboks have inspired a nation.
Producer: Stenette Grosskopf | Presenter: Govan Whittles

Script:



SPRINGBOKS HOMECOMING SCRIPT


V/O
It was a night few of us will ever forget. 80 minutes of collective nail-biting and breath-holding… And when the final whistle blew… we were rugby world champions again!
Siya lifting cup


V/O
Last Saturday the Springboks made history as they lifted the Webb Ellis trophy for the fourth time after edging out the New Zealand All Blacks with a single point.
UPS: Commentator SS
“Back to back and now 4 times Rugby World Champions!”
V/O
And South Africa has been celebrating ever since…




V/O
Tuesday morning, thousands of excited fans gather at OR Thambo International to welcome their heroes home…. And of course I am one of them!


Govan
The atmosphere here is electric!
Voxies
Bokke! World Champions!

Siya K olisi, we’re so proud. Rassie Erasmus, you’ve done magic for us as a nation.

Bokke, you did it for the continent.

Magic, 111.
111, we’ll call it a lucky Nelson from now on.
Absolutely.


V/O
It’s impossible not to get swept up by the exuberance of the colourful crowd…

4 times world champions. Undisputed…
World cup rugby champions of the world.
V/O
My challenge for the morning is to get through the crowd to the front…
Govan
It’s tight, you almost can't walk. I’m gonna make some space.
Govan
Oh I hate to push through but I have to
Voxies
It’s getting wild. Can’t wait to get the bokke back.

Kolisi for president, but I’m just hoping to see Faf

No space?
No space. .
Govan
Looks like this is as far as I am gonna go… I’m going to end up playing 8th man.
V/O
But I’m not giving up on finding the perfect spot.


Govan
Do you hear that… They say the Springboks have gone through customs, the passports have been stamped.. At any moment now they’re gonna come through those doors and this place is going to absolutely erupt … oof. We’re ready?
V/O
These final minutes feel like hours, but I find a friend on the opposite side of the aisle to help pass the time.
Rugby…


V/O
And then… there they are.. The heroes of a nation.
Siya Kolisi
It didn’t feel real until we came home. Coming to OR Thambo made us realise who we’re doing it for and why we’re doing it and I think that was the best thing in the world to see so many people at the airport. Because we knew you wanted a win, so that was very special.
Jody Hendricks
That moment when Siya Kolisi came through customs and ran into the crowd and lifted the trophy, just showed what it meant for not only the team, but also for the people of the country.
V/O
Jody Hendricks is a rugby commentator and writer…


Govan: What did you think, not necessarily the final game, but what did you think of the fact that we won again?

Jody: Four time world champions has a nice ring to it, doesn't it? I think the team did fantastically well. I think the fact that we won the last three games by one point showed the tenacity and showed that the team knew how to win games at crucial times.

T he experience of the team, remember, it's the nucleus of 2019. A lot of the players that won the previous cup was in this team as well, and that gave us the edge over other teams like New Zealand in a final. And it’s good to say that every time we’ve been in a World Cup final, we’ve won it.




V/O
Wednesday, the World Champions spent the day at MultiChoice for an in-house bash, soaking up every moment of the celebrations.
Frans Malherbe
It’s a really amazing experience to see the support and all our people welcoming us back.
Handré Pollard
I don’t think we really, really understand yet what we did, so I’m sure over the next few days when we tour SA we’re gonna get a good sense of what we did and … it’s just unbelievable.
Jody Hendricks
Govan: What do you think the symbolism is of the Springboks winning the World Cup in 2023 for South Africans?

Jody: I think it has definitely united the nation and I can use a lot of clichés. But if you look back at the history, more than a hundred years of the Springbok a lot of stigma around the apartheid era and who was allowed to be picked and who wasn't allowed to be. Now all of a sudden we have a team that has won back to back Rugby World Cups with sandwiched in between that is a Lions victory against the British and Irish Lions, and I think that has catapulted them to the best Springbok team of all time.



V/O
And their recipe for success is quite simple, it seems…
Trevor Nyakane
I think the way we buy into our game plan… The way we agree with whatever strategy the coaches come up with, 7-1, 6-2, whatever… we just buy in and i think that’s been the secret of the whole thing…
Lukhanyo Am
Being able to unite and be cohesive in the team, shows you can reach so much greatness when you’re like that.
Jody Hendricks
Govan: When Siya came home, he talked about how the Springbok victory had inspired a nation. How do you think that message lands?

Jody: I think the example that the Springboks have set with a slogan Stronger Together has shown not only South Africans but the world. What can be done when we work together. And I think one or two things that the government can learn is maybe a good question to ask is how many rugby fields or stadiums has the government built since the last Rugby World Cup in 2019, you know, to promote, to show that we are actually investing in this winning product that we've got called the Springboks.

The country, like Siya correctly said, has a lot of challenges. I mean, a day after they won the World Cup, the new loadshedding schedule came out – crime, corruption and everything like that. We've got our challenges, but we've got to learn when something goes right and maybe implement that in other parts of society as well.
V/O
On Thursday the Sprinkboks kicked off a 4-day national victory tour…
Voxie
New hope for the new future, for a new generation. We are here, Bokke!
V/O
… and scenes from Braamfontein in Johannesburg set the tone for more celebrations across the country.


Jody hendricks
Govan: The game has to go on, right? And Jacques Nienaber is leaving. Are you worried about that?

Jody: Well he just won a world cup, so I think any team would miss a World Cup winning coach. He’s of course going to Leinster in Ireland to join their coaching staff. So the debate is up as to who will replace him as the new Springbok coach. Rassie Erasmus told the media that he's not too worried, he'll be the interim coach. There's no rush to get a new coach, but from what I hear, it's Mzwandile Stick who's currently the assistant coach. He’s the favorite. A guy like Johan Ackermann, who had success with the Lions a couple of years ago, he's an option. And also Deon Davids was currently in charge of the forwards at the Springbok team, he has an outside chance….


V/O
Whatever the future holds, for now the Springboks are Kings of the world!




PROMO 1 21”


PROMO 2 21”
UPS: Man, it feels like Madiba is coming out of prison!

Thousands of Springbok fans, side-by-side, to give our World Champions the homecoming they deserve!

UPS: Siya was right….



PROMO 3 21”
8 days of non-stop celebration for the heroes of our nation!

UPS: hier kom die bokke

As South Africans live it up, basking in the glory of our fourth Rugby World Cup win, we look at what the future holds for the Springboks…

UPS: I think that has catapulted them to the best Springbok team of all time…
